extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers and anyone interested in film censorship and history
extracted.subtask_description: A country-by-country compiled list and explanatory notes of films that have been explicitly prohibited from public screening, including the stated grounds and administrative or legal actions that produced the bans. It documents reasons (political, moral, religious, legal, safety), responsible bodies, and temporal scope where known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion for list
rubrics_metrics.description: This list includes only films that have been explicitly prohibited from public screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude films that were merely edited to obtain a lower rating; also omit countries where films are banned on a wide scale (those large-scale bans are not listed in this table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: political reasons / political criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Films have been banned for political reasons, including criticism of governments, leaders, or political systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: films banned under dictatorships or regimes (e.g., many titles banned during Argentina's 'Argentine Revolution' or Brazil's military dictatorship), or movies critical of colonial rule or military actions (e.g., Afrique 50, Paths of Glory, The Battle of Algiers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: moral / obscenity / pornographic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned for being 'obscene', 'pornographic', or containing explicit sexual content deemed unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Last Tango in Paris, In the Realm of the Senses, Pretty Baby, Salò. Sometimes cited as 'violating morality standards' or 'obscenity'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: sexual content involving minors / child pornography concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans citing child pornography or sexual content involving minors (or simulated minors) as the primary concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Pretty Baby, Kindergarten; severe legal actions including seizure of copies and court orders have been used in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: religious offence / blasphemy / depiction of prophets
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned for blasphemy or for depicting religious figures in ways considered offensive or forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Last Temptation of Christ, The Da Vinci Code, Noah, The Prince of Egypt; bans sometimes initiated by religious groups or courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: LGBT content / homosexuality / transgender representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned because they 'promote homosexuality', include LGBT characters, or display LGBT symbols/messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Barbie (Algeria: 'promotes homosexuality'), Eternals, Thor: Love and Thunder, Lightyear (brief lesbian kiss), Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (transgender flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: inciting violence or civil unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned for allegedly inciting violence, unrest, or public disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Kite Runner banned in Afghanistan 'due to inciting violence'; some films withdrawn around sensitive anniversaries (Child 44 withdrawn around Victory Day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: negative portrayal of nation/people/army
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans based on a film's negative depiction of a country's people, armed forces, institutions, or national history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Red Zone Cuba, films banned for portraying Soviets/Russians poorly, or for 'harming the Congolese army's image'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: inaccurate or distorted depiction of historical events
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned for distorting historical facts or presenting history in a way authorities consider unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Child 44 withdrawn for 'distortion of historical facts'; Exodus: Gods and Kings banned for historical inaccuracies and perceived Zionist viewpoint in some countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: depiction of sensitive local culture / negative cultural portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for portraying local culture negatively, portraying locations or peoples as villainous, or insulting cultural norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: No Escape (negative portrayal of local culture), Kingsman: The Golden Circle (portraying Cambodia as antagonist base).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: national security / foreign relations concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans motivated by potential harm to diplomatic relations, international standing, or national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Born American banned for being 'potentially harmful to international relations'; films withheld to avoid offending allied nations (One, Two, Three and Finlandization example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: copyright/estate/legal claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans or confiscations resulting from copyright infringement or lawsuits by estates/individuals claiming rights violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Carmen Jones (technical copyright issue), Beyond Citizen Kane, Love Strange Love (lawsuit by an actress).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: depiction of real persons / defamation/privacy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned or blocked due to alleged violation of a real person's rights, privacy, or portrayal (e.g., use of images from funerals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Di Cavalcanti was confiscated after a family member alleged the painter's image was violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: portrayal of an ethnic/national group positively or negatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans triggered by how ethnic or national groups are portrayed (either positively or sympathetically in politically sensitive contexts, or negatively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Azerbaijan banned Hostage for presenting Armenians in a positive light; films critical of colonialism or sympathetic to insurgents have been banned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: depictions that could inspire copycat crimes or wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Films banned because authorities feared they would teach or inspire criminal acts (e.g., detailed crimes or techniques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Rififi banned for depiction of cracking security safes; other bans have cited fears of copycat crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: content harmful to mental health / excessively disturbing
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for being 'cruel, disturbing', potentially hazardous to mental health, or excessively violent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Human Centipede 2 (temporary ban), The Devils (banned citing potential mental health hazard), A Serbian Film (called an 'excuse for pedophilia' and extreme violence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative mechanism: government-appointed or private censor boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Many countries use government-appointed or private commissions to censor and rate productions; such bodies can ban, refuse classification, or demand cuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents multiple national censor boards and classification decisions, including refusals of classification that amount to practical bans (e.g., Ken Park refused classification in Australia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative mechanism: refusal of classification vs edited release
rubrics_metrics.description: Films may be refused classification (effectively banned) or allowed only in an edited/censored version; refusal vs conditional release is an important distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In the Realm of the Senses had censored versions then later full release; many films were banned until cuts were made, then reclassified and released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal mechanism: court orders and lawsuits can impose bans
rubrics_metrics.description: Court injunctions, legal suits, and judicial rulings are used to ban or seize films or copies in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Kindergarten seizure and court order; Borrando a papá prevented commercial premiere due to a court measure; some bans overturned by courts later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal variability of bans
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans can be temporary, era-specific, or lifted after changes in law/regime; the date ranges given show bans and later lifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Salò banned 1975–1992 in Australia then lifted; many titles banned under dictatorships later unbanned after regime change or law changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ban: national, regional, or platform-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans differ in scope: national bans, regional/city-level bans, or platform-specific blocks (cinema, TV, DVD, streaming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Some films banned from theatrical exhibition but allowed on DVD/online; others banned from television broadcasts; Hong Kong/HK-China film restrictions differ from mainland China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural/religious sensitivity: prohibition of depiction of sacred figures or norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Bans grounded in prohibitions against visual depiction of religious figures, or scenes that violate locally held religious norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Emigrant caused protests because Islam forbids visual depiction of religious figures; other films banned for offending religious sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic or political triggers: memes or imagery linked to political leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Films may be banned for containing imagery or references that are politically sensitive or associated with political criticism (even via memes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Winnie-the-Pooh films banned in mainland China because of a meme comparison with Xi Jinping; even parody/horror films referencing Pooh are blocked.
